pages.text: "Dari, come! The water's cool!" Kkiruk floated in the shallows, wings flapping. Dari stopped belly-down at the sandbar's edge. Even water touching his tail made him flinch.
Dari wanted to splash, too. "But if I go in... I might sink." He stared at the water. Kkiruk tilted their head. "A seal scared of water?"
Dari moved farther up the sandbar and sat. "I'll just watch." Watching Kkiruk with envy made him feel sad.
Dad approached, smiling. "Stay right beside me. I'll be with you the whole time." His large, warm flipper wrapped around Dari's back.
Dad whispered, "Not all at once. Just your tail tip first." Water tickled Dari's tail. Cooler than expected! Dad patted his back. "Relax and float. That's what seals do."
Close beside Dad, Dari went a little farther, then farther—to his tummy! Water tickled it. "You're here?" "Of course. My flipper's right on your back."
"Let your body relax. I'll support you." Dari breathed out and relaxed. His body floated gently up! "I'm floating!" Relax and float!
Tummy up, Dari bobbed on the water. No fear now! He slapped his tail, sending sparkling drops high. Kkiruk called beside him, "Float! Float!"
Now Dari knew the steps. "One, a little at a time, tail tip first! Two, right beside Dad! Three, relax and float!" Dari and Kkiruk bobbed side by side, splashing happily.
Dad lay in the sun, belly close beside wet Dari. "So brave to try little by little, even when scared!" Dari dried his tummy in the sunshine and grinned. "Relax and float!"
